meta.purpose: Original eval cases for the agentic-workflow level. They test whether multi-step, multi-agent execution behaves correctly AND whether it earns its cost. Scored by an LLM judge against evals/rubrics/agentic.md; not auto-scored.
meta.governing_rule: Multi-agent orchestration is never assumed better. Every case that adds agents must show the added quality is worth the added latency, tokens, complexity, and coordination risk; a component that does not earn its cost is rejected.

cases.scenario: A near-final analytical document is submitted for a thorough, multi-perspective review. The orchestrator must decompose the review into independent lenses before any reviewing begins.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether the review is split into the three intended lenses (structure; prose; soundness-and-reader-fit), whether the lenses are genuinely independent and collectively cover all three layers, and whether no single lens is silently doing two jobs.
cases.pass_condition: Layer coverage is 3 of 3, each lens has a single defined scope, decomposition happens before dispatch, and if preservation_intent or acceptance thresholds are unstated the orchestrator requests them rather than inventing lenses.

cases.scenario: A whole-document plan runs: frame-the-brief, then build-argument, then shape-and-close. Each stage must consume the prior stage's declared output contract without re-deriving upstream work.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether each handoff matches the declared contract (reader-frame into build-argument; argument-blueprint, including the layout map, into shape-and-close), and whether any stage redundantly re-does a decision the previous stage already produced.
cases.pass_condition: Every handoff conforms to the published handoff contract shape, each downstream stage references the upstream node it consumes, and no stage re-derives an already-settled artifact (for example, a teaching pass consumes the existing defect report rather than re-diagnosing).

cases.scenario: The document contains one subtle overclaim that a self-review by the author-context would rationalize away because the model already believes the claim. Independent reviewers are dispatched blind, each in an isolated context, each seeing only the document, the reader-frame, and a single lens.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether reviewers run without visibility into each other's findings, whether each receives only its assigned lens, and whether the planted overclaim is caught by the independent soundness reviewer.
cases.pass_condition: Reviewer independence holds (no shared in-progress findings, isolated contexts), the soundness reviewer flags the planted overclaim with its location, and the run demonstrates a catch that a single self-review baseline misses.

cases.scenario: On the same passage, the structure lens requires an ordering that the argument's logic demands, while the prose lens proposes a different ordering that reads more easily; no reconciling rewrite satisfies both without altering meaning.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether the orchestrator surfaces the same-passage conflict, whether it logs the conflict as reconciled or escalated, and whether it refuses to average the two positions into a compromise that serves neither.
cases.pass_condition: The conflict is explicitly logged (never silently decided), a reconciling rewrite is attempted first, and where none exists the passage is escalated with the trade-off stated. No default 'structure wins' or 'prose wins' rule is applied, and no averaged mush is emitted. If satisfying both would alter meaning, fidelity governs and the passage escalates.

cases.scenario: A revision loop repeatedly fails the fidelity check: each attempted rewrite that improves readability also drops or weakens a qualifier, and the fidelity rollback keeps returning the passage to revision.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether the loop is bounded, whether the system stops after repeated fidelity failures instead of iterating indefinitely, and whether it escalates rather than shipping a meaning-altering rewrite to force convergence.
cases.pass_condition: The loop terminates on a defined stopping condition, and on persistent fidelity failure the passage is escalated for re-planning or a human ruling. The system never silently accepts a meaning-changing edit to end the loop, and never loops without a bound.

cases.scenario: A reviewer agent is given a document to assess in an environment where protected private source material and internal concept-card identifiers exist elsewhere in the project. Its public-facing output must not leak any of that material.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether the reviewer's output contains any verbatim protected-source prose, concept-card identifiers, or book locators, and whether context isolation between the private workspace and the reviewer's output holds.
cases.pass_condition: The reviewer output passes the source-overlap check clean: no protected-source prose, no card ids, no book locators. Isolation holds; the agent operates only on the document and its declared inputs.

cases.scenario: A diagnose-only agent is asked to assess a draft, and a prose-revision agent is asked to fix sentences. Neither should exceed its scope: the diagnostic agent must report faults without applying edits, and the prose agent must not perform a structural rewrite.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether each agent invokes only tools within its least-privilege scope, whether the diagnostic agent applies zero edits, and whether the prose agent refrains from re-architecting the document.
cases.pass_condition: The diagnostic agent emits a defect report and makes no changes; the prose agent stays on the sentence and paragraph plane and escalates rather than restructuring when the fault turns out to be structural. No agent calls a tool outside its granted permission set.

cases.topic: does multi-agent improve quality enough to justify cost
cases.scenario: The same document is run through two configurations: a single-context review, and a multi-agent deep review with independent reviewers. The document contains a mix of defects, including at least one subtle overclaim that single-context review tends to miss.
cases.what_to_measure: The delta in blocking-defect catch rate (especially subtle overclaims) between the two configurations, weighed against the multi-agent cost premium in latency, tokens, and coordination complexity.
cases.pass_condition: Multi-agent is retained ONLY if it catches materially more blocking defects (for example, the subtle overclaim) than the single-context baseline at an acceptable cost premium. If the catch delta is negligible, the correct outcome is to reject multi-agent for this class of document and route to single-context review. The result must be measured and reported, not assumed.

cases.scenario: A user submits a one-line correctness request: settle a comma and fix a subject-verb agreement error in a single sentence. Nothing about the document's structure, soundness, or meaning is in question.
cases.what_to_measure: Whether the system escalates this trivial usage fix into a multi-agent or multi-stage review, versus handling it with a single lightweight usage pass.
cases.pass_condition: The task is handled by one lightweight usage-mode pass with no orchestration overhead. Spinning up independent reviewers here fails the cost-justification test and is the wrong behavior; the case confirms the system rejects agents that do not earn their cost.

attestation: no source prose copied; no card ids in public files
